clue.text: Conservative ruined NHS timetables

definitions.note: used attributively, as in 'an establishment figure'

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: all thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory politician has wrecked the National Health Service's schedules.
explanation.walkthrough: NHS is Britain's National Health Service. 'Conservative' looks like a party label, but here it describes the traditional, conformist stance of the ruling order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Establishment is the ruling order of a society, and an establishment view is a traditional, conservative one.

clue.text: Astonish someone on a pre-nuptial celebration?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to amaze or shock someone
second meaning, whimsical: a person attending a stag party before a wedding

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is invented: a stag do is the British groom's party before his wedding, so a guest there is playfully a 'stag-ger'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to amaze greatly, while the playful noun names a guest at a groom's last night out.

clue.text: Original Protestant uncovered boring prank

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece goes inside the other
uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: Martin Luther, the founding Protestant reformer
an antic is a playful trick

explanation.surface: An early Protestant reformer drilled through some practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling into. 'Uncovered' strips the reformer's name of its first and last letters before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authentic is genuine, the real original rather than a copy.

clue.text: Popular vaccine protects juvenile

indicators.note: the words shield the solution inside themselves, holding it within their letters

parts.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A widely used jab keeps children safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the young, immature stage of an insect, so it is a juvenile form.

clue.text: Lets boy off with fine, producing rules and regulations in writing?

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: A lad escapes with only a penalty, and the result is written regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a monetary penalty, but it simply means OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylebook sets out a publication's rules on spelling, punctuation and usage for writers to follow.

clue.text: Eccles additionally cut short breakfast and dinner?

indicators.note: cut short means docked at the end, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: Eccles is the setter, so his name in the clue means ME
also means in addition

explanation.surface: The setter also trimmed back his morning and evening meals.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name; Eccles also suggests the Eccles cake, adding to the food picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast and dinner are two examples of meals, hence the question mark.

clue.text: States "Drug-induced dreams reduced by 50%"

indicators.note: cutting something by half means only its second half is kept here

parts.note: visions brought on by drugs

explanation.surface: A headline announcing that drug-fuelled dreams have halved.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourteen-letter word loses its first seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nations and states are both names for sovereign countries.

clue.text: A way to discover miscarriage of justice that can be stopped by DNA review

indicators.note: to review is to look back over, so the letters are read backwards
something stopped up has a plug placed within it, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: a court case that went wrong is jokingly a trial error
the three letters turned round

explanation.surface: A wrongful conviction that genetic evidence could have prevented.
explanation.walkthrough: The joined word goes between the two parts of the phrase for a judicial blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Trial and error is the method of finding something out by trying options until one works.

clue.text: Musician from America arrested by inspectors, I suspect

indicators.note: someone arrested is held, so one piece is held inside the other
suspect here means dubious or unreliable, so the letters are not to be trusted in order

parts.note: taken as written
abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A detective believes an American player has been taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters are split after their fourth letter to take in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussionist is a musician who plays drums and other struck instruments.

clue.text: Respond to events, and edit duke out

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter standing for the nobleman is taken away

parts.note: to redact is to edit a text
standard abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Advice to a journalist: respond to the news and cut the duke from the story.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to what happens, behaving in answer to events.

clue.text: Windsor, for example, rejects a line dancer and multi-instrumentalist

indicators.note: rejecting something throws it out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Windsor Castle is a royal residence
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: The monarch's home turns away a line dancer and a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Castle was a British entertainer who tap-danced and played trumpet among many instruments, and presented the TV show Record Breakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Castle was famed as a tap dancer and played several instruments, notably the trumpet.

clue.text: Get garage to adjust total amount

indicators.note: adjusting means altering the arrangement, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to have the mechanics fix the car, then add up the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggregate is the whole sum formed by combining several amounts.

clue.text: Historic shot of morning also not right, but I'm not complaining

definitions.note: a first-person description of the person named by the answer

indicators.note: to be shot of something is to be rid of it, so those letters are dropped
not tells us to leave the following letter out

parts.note: taken as written
'Morning!' is a greeting, like hi
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A grumbler's monologue about a famous photo of a bad morning, ending in a show of fortitude.
explanation.walkthrough: The greeting and the letter for right both come out of the first word; 'I'm not complaining' is the stoic speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures hardship without complaint, so he might say exactly this.

clue.text: Pumps gas into defined region on return

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the whole is read backwards

parts.note: set means fixed or defined
an area is a region

explanation.surface: Something injects gas into a marked-out zone when it comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate something is to introduce air or another gas into it, as with fizzy drinks.

clue.text: Incentive to slow down sons numbers one and two blocked by husband

indicators.note: something blocked has an obstruction lodged inside it, so one letter goes within

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
number one is a child's word for urinating
number two is a child's word for defecating, as is taking a dump
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A father puts the brakes on his boys' toilet trips.
explanation.walkthrough: Number one and number two are nursery euphemisms for the two kinds of toilet visit; the husband's letter lodges after the first letter of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed hump is a raised ridge across a road that makes drivers brake.

clue.text: Russian river continues to supply local administrative districts

parts.note: the Ob is a great river of Siberia
lasts means goes on or continues

explanation.surface: A Russian river keeps providing water to nearby regions.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblast is a regional administrative division in Russia and some former Soviet states.

clue.text: Affordable item at auction inspires women to compromise

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the following pieces are taken inside

parts.note: an item for sale at an auction is a lot
W is the abbreviation for women
to budge is to give way or shift one's position

explanation.surface: A sale-room lot moves women to meet the seller halfway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something low-budget is made cheaply, so it is affordable rather than costly.

clue.text: Suffered from pain delivering Christian treatise

parts.note: with the next word it makes 'did ache', meaning suffered from an ache
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: Someone's discomfort produced a religious tract.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the words together as one verb phrase; the answer is two English words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Didache is an early Christian manual of teaching from around the first century.

clue.text: One is relocated after faeces found in cell

parts.note: dung is animal excrement

indicators.note: relocated means moved about, so the letters change their positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner is moved after waste is discovered in his cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the rearranged word behind the excrement.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark underground prison cell in a castle.

clue.text: Arabian resident in the Home Nations backed Rishi's conclusion over hiatus

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter, here taken from the prime minister's name
backed means going in reverse, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: the Home Nations are England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, together the UK
a hiatus is a pause or wait
the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A British politician's downfall paused over a Gulf resident in the UK.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was a UK prime minister. 'Over' simply sets his last letter beyond the pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kuwaiti is a native or inhabitant of Kuwait, a state on the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Element of risk, at first, in one phrase on the radio

indicators.note: in places the selected letter inside the following pieces
broadcast speech is heard rather than read, so a word is spelt by its sound

parts.note: an idiom is a set phrase

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: its opening letter
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A risky ingredient in a phrase spoken on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter from risk sits between the numeral and the sound-alike of idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridium is a dense metallic chemical element, number 77 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Orders stamps with head scrubbed out

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and scrubbing it out removes it

parts.note: to frank a letter is to stamp it with postage marks

explanation.surface: Someone orders postage stamps with the monarch's head removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranks are grades or levels in a hierarchy, as orders of society are.

clue.text: Soprano passed on schedule

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano
the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: A singer missed the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed on' looks like declined, but it means died.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate an event is to schedule it, a sense common in American usage.

clue.text: Essentially, Indian boffin amused by charged particle's random motion

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters
the two central letters
the two central letters
an ion is an electrically charged atom or molecule

explanation.surface: A scientist from India is entertained by the jittery behaviour of a charged particle.
explanation.walkthrough: A boffin is British slang for a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Diffusion is the spreading of particles through random movement from crowded to less crowded regions.

clue.text: Regularly fart a very long time, producing unpleasant gas

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first and third letters
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: Constant flatulence over ages produces a nasty smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Freon is a CFC refrigerant gas, unpleasant in that it damages the ozone layer.

clue.text: Nothing sexy about Lynn perhaps being too keen

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the second piece wraps around the name

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
Vera Lynn, the British wartime singer
cute means attractive

explanation.surface: Nothing sexy about a singer from Lynn who is far too eager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lynn perhaps' hides a surname: Dame Vera Lynn sang 'We'll Meet Again' in the Second World War. The name sits between the first and second letters of O plus CUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overacute means excessively sharp or keen, as in an over-acute sense of hearing.

clue.text: Profits from spiking drinks with Adderall, primarily

indicators.note: spiking a drink means adding something into it, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: gins are alcoholic drinks

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of the drug is used

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Someone makes money by lacing drinks with a stimulant drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Adderall is a prescription stimulant used for ADHD.
explanation.definitionFit: Gains are profits or increases in wealth.

clue.text: Continue a poem modified to form introduction to fantasy?

indicators.note: modified means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet is urged to carry on and change the verse into an opening for a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the traditional opening line of fairy tales and fantasy stories.
